title: Pizza Siciliana
subtitle: Thick Sicilian-style pizza with tomatoes, anchovies, capers, and olives
excerpt: Pizza siciliana (sfincione) is the original Sicilian pizza: a thick, spongy bread base topped with a cooked tomato and onion sauce, anchovies, capers, black olives, and a bread-crumb topping. It is quite different from Neapolitan or Roman pizza: closer to focaccia with toppings than to a thin-crust pizza: and it is eaten throughout Sicily as street food and at home.
sourceNotes: Sfincione is the traditional Sicilian pizza, originating in Palermo. The name comes from the Latin spongiosus (spongy), referring to the thick bread base. It is documented in Sicilian culinary history from at least the 17th century. The Palermitano version uses anchovy, capers, and olives; other Sicilian versions vary by region.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dough can be made 24 hours ahead and cold-proved in the fridge. The tomato sauce can also be made ahead. Assemble and bake on the day.

content.text: Pizza siciliana: known in Palermo as sfincione: is a thick-based pizza, more bread than flatbread, baked in a rectangular tin. The topping is a cooked tomato and onion sauce with anchovies, capers, and black olives, finished with breadcrumbs that toast to a golden crust. It is eaten at room temperature as much as hot and is a Sicilian street food in the same category as arancini.

Mix the flour, salt, and yeast in a large bowl. Add the warm water and olive oil and mix to a sticky dough. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and very elastic. The dough should be softer and stickier than standard bread dough. Cover and prove for 2 hours at room temperature until doubled.

Oil a 35 x 25 cm baking tin generously. Tip in the dough and press with oiled fingers to fill the tin. It may spring back: cover and leave for 30 minutes, then press again. Leave to prove in the tin for another 30 minutes.

While the dough proves, cook the onions in 2 tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes until very soft and golden. Add the tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens. Season and cool slightly.

Heat the oven to 220°C fan. Spread the tomato and onion sauce over the proved dough. Press the anchovies into the surface. Scatter over the capers and olives. Mix the breadcrumbs with 2 tablespoons of olive oil and scatter over the top.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the breadcrumbs are golden and the base is cooked through. The edges should be crisp. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes before cutting.

items.symptom: Base is doughy and undercooked in the centre
items.cause: Oven temperature too low or baking time too short for a thick base
items.fix: Bake at full 220°C and check the base by lifting a corner with a palette knife: it should be golden underneath. Add 5 more minutes if needed.

items.symptom: Topping is wet and doesn't hold
items.cause: Tomato sauce was not reduced enough before applying
items.fix: The sauce should be thick and dark before spreading: it will continue releasing moisture in the oven, so starting thick is essential.

items.symptom: Breadcrumbs burn before the base is cooked
items.cause: Too high in the oven or too much oil on the breadcrumbs
items.fix: Bake in the lower third of the oven. Cover loosely with foil if the top is browning too fast.

content.text: Sfincione is Palermo's iconic street food. It is sold in thick squares from market stalls and bakeries all over the city. It is linked to the Ballarò and Vucciria markets and eaten at any time of day. The Sicilian pantry flavours of anchovy and capers appear here as they do in caponata and stuffed vegetables.
